newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S RICHTER, GRABO IMPRESS AFTER Q1 RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S RICHTER, GRABO IMPRESS AFTER Q1 RESULTS.

text.p: Fast sales growth in Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union have kept Hungarian pharmaceuticals Richter Gedeon and home improvement products maker Graboplast among investors' favourites after their first quarter earnings, analysts said on Wednesday.
"Richter is more expensive than other pharmaceutical stocks but it has a very fast pace of growth and it is still undervalued," said Tommy Erdei, analyst at ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett in Budapest.

The company, which is ahead of a pricing probably on Thursday in the second phase of its privatisation, reported an IAS net profit of 4.997 billion forints for the first quarter of 1997, up from 3.258 billion in the same period of 1996.

Richter's sales to the CIS grew 40.1 percent to $22.7 percent as its sales to those countries benefited to some extent from an average price increase of four percent implemented at the beginning of January.

Graboplast, maintaining the high proportion (60 percent) of exports, has also benefited from continuous market expansion, particularly in eastern Europe, as well as from a strong management team, analysts said.
Graboplast reported a 28 percent rise in its HAS consolidated sales to 4.019 billion forints from 3.142 billion, maintaining the high, around 60 percent, proportion of exports.

"The 28 percent increase stems from a growth in volumes," said Andrea Dicso, analyst at Bank Austria-Investment Rt. "The company did not raise its prices (in Q1), this means that its market expansion continues."
The group's after-tax profit grew to 475.5 million forints from 215.5 million in the same period of 1996.
"Graboplast performed very well (in Q1) despite the fact that its weakest quarter is traditionally the first three months," Dicso said.

"I expect a significant increase in the second quarter, possibly coupled with minor price increases," she said, adding she expected the third quarter, Graboplast's main season, to bring an "exceptionally significant increase."
The icing on the cake for Graboplast was its two billion forints cash reserves which can be spent for example for acquisitions, she added.

ABN AMRO Hoare Govett's Erdei noted an increase in exports by Hungary's other large pharmaceuticals maker Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt , but held back from recommending the share because of a drop in its domestic sales.

"I wouldn't recommend it for investments until they can at least maintain domestic sales at (unchanged) levels," he said. "The important is that Egis should try to stabilise its domestic market and maintain the quick pace of export growth."

Egis, majority owned by France's Servier S.A., reported quarterly exports of $19.9 million which showed a 35 percent rise in dollar terms over the same period of 1996, bolstered by a 50 percent export growth to CIS countries. However, Egis's domestic sales fell 13 percent from the same period of 1996.
In 1996 domestic sales accounted for 54.9 percent of Egis's total sales and the company expected this ratio to drop to 52 percent in 1997 and to below 50 percent in 1998.

Meanwhile retail chain Fotex Rt , which was hard hit by a consumer slump following Hungary's austerity measures launched in March 1995, may start to regain its strong profitability, following restructuring amid signs that Hungary may be entering a period of economic growth, they said.
Fotex reported an IAS consolidated net income of 163 million forints for the first three months, up from 71 million in the same period of last year.

"Late last year the company began to perform better and I think (1997) first quarter figures confirmed that," Erdei said, "Fotex is starting to be a very attractive stock. I guess (the improvement) stems more from Fotex's inner restructuring than from outer factors."

On the Budapest Stock Exchange on Wednesday Richter closed at 14,455 forints, down 225; Graboplast remained steady at 8,695 forints; Fotex gained four forints to end at 140; while Egis rose 50 forints to 10,850.
